excerpt: In a visuo-spatial attention task, TMS to IPS or FEF, but not pre-central gyrus, reduced typical anticipatory alpha decreases; IPS stimulation produced anticipatory increases. The degree of TMS disruption of alpha decreases was related to participants' response speed to targets.
overview: This evidence connects alpha gating to control regions rather than only to sensory cortex. Perturbing IPS and FEF changes anticipatory alpha dynamics and behavior, supporting a fronto-parietal mechanism for deploying alpha-mediated gating. Because the task differed from classic distracter-only designs, the result is best read as control-network evidence, not as proof that every alpha effect has the same spatial form.
title: Fronto-Parietal Control Evidence
